top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on a simple, general mechanism: at the magic wavelength the trap light shifts both clock levels equally, so many neutral atoms are held Doppler- and recoil-free without perturbing the line. It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, has been independently verified across laboratories at the 10^-18 level, and the two-name Katori and Ye allocation is defensible, with Katori holding priority and Ye establishing the many-atom systematics. The citation should be confined to invention and realization.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Chalmers colleagues Johansson and Olsson are in the same Gothenburg physics environment but no collaboration is recorded and no candidate is from that environment
